title: The Bass trace conjecture for group rings
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) of the Bass trace conjecture for complex group rings: for every group, the Hattori-Stallings trace of every finitely generated projective module over CG vanishes at the conjugacy classes of elements of infinite order. Consequences: for torsion-free groups the canonical trace of an idempotent matrix equals the rank of its augmentation, and the group ring over any commutative domain of characteristic zero has no idempotents other than 0 and 1 (Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture in characteristic zero); with Linnell's restriction, Bass's conjecture for integral group rings. The first lesson sets up the trace; the second and third build weighted path sums of an idempotent and simplicial cycles from them; the fourth constructs a Pfaffian cocycle with value 2^-m times the trace coefficient and proves the theorem from a vanishing theorem for sparse cycles. Lessons five to eight prove that vanishing theorem: a transport metric with small balls, equivariant separating filtrations over a free parameter space, near-minimal separators with few zero strata, and chain maps built from the filtrations. The ninth draws the consequences and proves Linnell's restriction by a congruence for traces of p-th powers.

checks.reading: The manuscript 'The Bass trace conjecture for complex group rings' (OpenAI, 24 Sep 2026; sections 01-introduction to 10-torsion-free; local clone openai-math-20261006) was read in full on 15 Oct 2026, and every step was checked while the lessons were written: subgroup locality, the kernel identity, path weights and the twisted shift, the deletion identities, the even-dimensional cycles and their connected supports, the relative exponents, the Pfaffian rotation identity and the recurrence, lift independence and the cocycle identity of the detector, the transport metric and the branch functions, local finiteness, the tree volumes and gradient bounds, the connected-set count and the volume margin, the free parameter space, compatible cuts, existence of filtrations, the iterated dimension drop and the carriers, near-minimality, the disjoint replacements and the orbit-counting identity, the slicing inequality and the iteration, the component labels, the chain maps, the flag count, the equivariant homotopy, the assembly, the torsion-free corollary and the integral corollary. No error found. Changes of form in the course: the invariant probability on the parameter space is a finitely additive content on clopen sets, all integrals being finite sums; inequalities that hold outside countably many levels are integrated with Riemann sums whose tags avoid the exceptional levels; the facts on polyhedra (vertices of bounded polyhedra, coning triangulations, cells cut out by hyperplanes, subdivision chains of a triangulated simplex) are proved; Linnell's restriction, cited in the manuscript from Berrick-Hesselholt, is proved in lesson 9 by a congruence for traces of p-th powers of integral matrices (necklaces of words and Fermat's congruence modulo prime powers). The companion manuscript 'The l1-Bass Conjecture for Discrete Groups' (5 Oct 2026) was read in its introduction and its reduction section; its theorem is stated in lesson 9, not proved. Later literature, read on 15 Oct 2026 in arXiv searches ('Bass conjecture'; 'idempotent conjecture'; 'Hattori-Stallings'; 'Kadison-Kaplansky'; 'Bass trace'; 'separating filtration'; 'Uryson width'; Kaplansky AND idempotent; 'group ring' AND idempotent): Ta arXiv:2610.20306 and Elhamdadi-Ta-Virgin arXiv:2609.03799 are cited; OpenAI's Kadison-Kaplansky manuscript (23 Sep 2026) is cited from its introduction. Path sums of idempotents e = f - f a (1 - f) and conjugates by 1 + n with n^2 = 0, over the infinite dihedral group, the Heisenberg group and Z x S3 (lengths 1 to 5, up to 6,560 orbits): twisted-shift invariance, all deletion identities, total weight equal to the trace coefficient; Pfaffians: matching formula = exterior definition, expansion along the last index, permutation sign, the twisted rotation identity (sizes 2, 4, 6); the relative-exponent function of the Heisenberg group with central g equals the orbit construction and satisfies its three rules; psi_1, psi_2 lift independent and cocycles; psi_1 = -1 on the torus cycle; the congruence r(A^(p^k)) = psi^p r(A^(p^(k-1))) mod p^k for random integral matrices over H3(Z), D_inf, D16, S4, Z x S3 (p = 2, 3, 5; up to 336 coefficients where the two sides differ by multiples of p^k); connected-set counts below D^(2n) on Z^2 and the 3-regular tree; the margin n_0(D) = 274, 3283, 16416, 53950, 138598 for D = 2..6; the parameter space for S3 (41,472 points) and Z/6 (23,328 points): defining rule, invariance, free action.

The l1 theorem of the companion manuscript (OpenAI, 5 Oct 2026) is stated in lesson 9 and not proved; a follow-up course is recorded in plan/OPENAI_207_SCOPING_20261015.md.
